articles.title: Judge orders Élections Québec to prepare voter reminder cards in French and English
articles.summary: A Quebec judge has ordered Élections Québec to prepare voter information cards in both English and in French, in a civil court judgment issued Wednesday morning.

image.caption: Élections Québec announced earlier this month that it would only send voter information documents in French this year to comply with Quebec's language laws. (Graham Hughes/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Montreal·Breaking
A Quebec judge has ordered Élections Québec to prepare voter information cards in both English and in French, in a civil court judgment issued Wednesday morning.
Agency to be exempted from part of the Charter of the French Language for 10 days
· CBC News
· Posted: Sep 16, 2026 10:20 AM EDT | Last Updated: 12 minutes ago
A Quebec judge has ordered Élections Québec to prepare election reminder cards in English and in French, in a civil court judgment issued Wednesday morning.

The court was asked to grant a provisional interlocutory injunction and exempt the provincial agency from a section of Quebec's Charter of the French Language that makes French the only language of communication for public institutions.
In his decision, Judge Sylvain Lussier said he partially accepted the provisional interlocutory injunction, granting it for a period of 10 days.
Geoffrey Chambers is the plaintiff in the case. He's the former president of the Quebec Community Groups Network, known today as the TALQ.
Chambers filed the lawsuit after Élections Québec announced earlier this month that, for the first time in a general election, it would send out voter information cards solely in French.

items: Quebec won't reverse course on French-only voter info mailout ahead of provincial election

blocks.text: Élections Québec mails out three different documents to voters ahead of provincial elections: an election guide, a notice of entry and a reminder card.
The court said ordering Élections Québec to produce and mail an English version of the first two documents at this stage was “unrealistic and extremely costly.”

For now, the judge said he can only order the agency to prepare the reminder cards. Since the mail rollout for those documents falls outside the 10-day injunction period, another judicial process will be needed to order the actual mailing of the documents.
The reminder cards will include a list of candidates in the voter’s riding as well as details on where and when to vote. Quebecers head to the polls on Oct. 5.
Anglo seniors' right to vote compromised, judge says

In his decision, written in French, Lussier said it was obvious that "a great number" of anglophone seniors would not be able to exercise their right to vote in the absence of "comprehensible information."
He pointed to the recent federal election in Terrebonne, where a single miscounted vote nullified the results.
"Is it in the public interest to urgently deprive the English-speaking community of Quebec of the right it has always enjoyed to receive election information in English?," reads Lussier's judgment.
"To ask the question is to answer it."

Earlier this month, a spokesperson for Élections Québec, Julie St-Arnaud Drolet, said the agency had pleaded to no avail with Quebec to be able to send basic voting information in both French and English.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Cassandra Yanez-Leyton is a journalist for CBC News based in Montreal. You can email her story ideas at cassandra.yanez-leyton@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Lanao del Sur governor backs Macacua’s continued leadership in BARMM
articles.summary: ILIGAN CITY— Lanao del Sur Gov. Mamintal Adiong Jr. has expressed his support for the continued leadership of Abdulraof Macacua as chief minister of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim…

blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY— Lanao del Sur Gov. Mamintal Adiong Jr. has expressed his support for the continued leadership of Abdulraof Macacua as chief minister of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) following the region’s first parliamentary elections.
Adiong, who also serves as secretary-general of the BARMM Grand Coalition (BGC), congratulated Macacua on what he described as his “decisive victory” in the historic elections held on Sept. 14.

The first regular Bangsamoro parliamentary elections filled 80 seats in the region’s regular parliament. Under the parliamentary system, the chief minister will be chosen by the newly elected parliament rather than directly by voters.

“I extend my warmest congratulations to Chief Minister Abdulraof ‘Sammy Gambar’ Macacua on his decisive victory in the historic first Bangsamoro parliamentary elections, and I am glad to reaffirm my personal and political support for his continued leadership as Chief Minister of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao,” Adiong said.
Adiong said he and Macacua had worked together in building the Bangsamoro region, including in regional governance and public service.
He said he has long believed that the region’s future would be better served by leaders who can build bridges across political differences.

“I know his sincerity, his discipline, and his love for the Bangsamoro, and I am confident that under his leadership, this new chapter of self-governance will be guided with wisdom and unity,” Adiong said.
He also said he believed his support for Macacua was shared by local leaders in Lanao del Sur.
As governor, Adiong said the province is ready to work with the Bangsamoro government under Macacua’s leadership to advance programs benefiting communities across the region.
Macacua’s Bangsamoro Federalist Party garnered 31 of 80 seats in the incoming regular Parliament, short of the number needed to form the regional government.

Adiong’s recent pronouncement raises the possibility that the BGC could form a coalition with the BFP, throwing its eight seats behind Macacua, along with six more seats won by his local party, SIAP. /mcm

articles.title: Bondi attacks prompt creation of new institute for emergency care of children in NSW
articles.summary:
NSW Institute for Paediatric Trauma will help doctors, researchers and specialists prepare for trauma cases

  • Get our

blocks.text: A new institute dedicated to improving emergency medical care for severely injured children will be established in New South Wales following recent high-profile trauma events in the state.

Based at the Sydney Children’s hospital in Randwick, the NSW Institute for Paediatric Trauma will bring together clinicians, researchers and specialists to deliver advanced training and simulations across the health system.
Expected to be operational within six months, the institute aims to prepare medical teams for complex paediatric trauma cases, from initial emergency treatment to long-term rehabilitation.
The NSW health minister, Ryan Park, said the initiative follows emergency responses to critical incidents in the state.

“The events that occurred at Bondi Beach and at Bondi Junction have forever left their mark on NSW,” Park said. “Seeing the way in which our frontline workers and clinicians responded to these events with such courage and professionalism was nothing short of remarkable.”
“We know we won’t always be able to prevent trauma events, but we can make sure we are ready to respond when children and families need us most.”
Medical experts stress that treating children requires distinct clinical approaches to treating adults.
Dr Guy Henry, co-director of trauma services at Randwick, said children’s bodies, injuries and clinical needs differ significantly from adult patients.

While adult trauma frequently involves assaults or motor vehicle accidents, paediatric admissions generally present distinct patterns, including internal organ injuries in adolescents taking physical risks, and a growing number of e-bike crashes.

“Burns is another issue with children, there’s a different pattern of burns in children compared to adults,” he said. “People need to be aware of the differences and need to know how to respond to those differences.”
Preparing for mass casualties

Henry, who attended to victims of the Westfield Bondi Junction stabbings in 2024 and the Bondi beach terror attack, said regular education and mass casualty simulations are essential for building response capabilities.

He cited the medical response to the 2017 Manchester Arena attack – where hospital staff had completed a mass casualty simulation six weeks before – as evidence of how practice improves outcomes during critical events.
after newsletter promotion

“Through education, including the use of simulation, we can make people more familiar with managing trauma, with something like a mass casualty that no one might have any experience with,” Henry said.
“We get people more familiar, a little bit more comfortable, and that will then make us improve on how we manage things.”

Training will initially be based at Randwick, with future plans to explore how the program can be expanded across regional NSW and into the ACT, which regularly transfers paediatric trauma cases to Sydney hospitals.
The institute also aims to extend education simulation training to pre-hospital first responders, including paramedics, firefighters, police and the State Emergency Service.
Beyond clinical care and injury prevention research, the institute will address the psychological toll on healthcare workers and affected families.

“It’s been identified that not only do we have the child that we have to manage, we have the families to manage, we also have our own staff to manage,” Henry said, noting that upskilling staff helps lessen the psychological trauma of critical events.

The institute will draw on expertise across the Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network – including the children’s hospital at Westmead and the Newborn and Paediatric Emergency Transport Service – and will complement the Agency for Clinical Innovation’s Institute of Trauma and Injury Management. Philanthropic support will be provided through the Sydney Children’s Hospitals Foundation.

articles.title: How the Houthis are also putting Egypt under pressure
articles.summary: The Houthis, a Yemeni rebel group, are expanding their control of maritime corridors in the Red Sea area. Their target is their avowed enemy Saudi Arabia. But the military moves also endanger Egypt.

image.caption: Waterway under pressure: the Suez Canal, here near Egypt's Ismailia provinceImage: Ahmed Gomaa/Xinhua/picture alliance

blocks.text: Any and all ships may pass, at least at first. That was how the spokesperson for Yemen's Houthis rebel militia put it. Transit through the Red Sea would be safe, with one exception: According to the Houthi spokesperson, ships from Saudi Arabia would not be allowed to pass this stretch of the sea.

The comments came during a time when the Houthi militia has been fighting to increase its presence at the southern entrance to the ocean passage. The Houthis now control the tiny volcanic island of Mayun, also known as Perim, at the entrance to the Red Sea, as well as other parts of the Yemeni coast and some small islands.
With these moves, pressure is growing on Saudi Arabia, the country that opposes the Houthis and previously fought a war (unsuccessfully) with them.
Red Sea strains rattle energy markets
But pressure is now also increasing in Egypt. Every decrease in shipping traffic through the Red Sea also impacts one of that country's most important sources of national income, the Suez Canal.

As yet, maritime traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has not been significantly reduced. According to news agency Reuters, last Saturday 24 ships passed through it and on Sunday, 27 did so. That is around the same as the 10-day average. The Houthis appear to want to signal that their plan is not stop traffic altogether. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is a chokepoint between Yemen and and the Horn of Africa. Ships have to pass it to enter the Red Sea.

blocks.caption: Boats that are not Saudi Arabian can still pass the Bab al-Mandeb Strait (file photo from April 2026)Image: REUTERS

blocks.text: In general though, maritime traffic has decreased here, according to maritime intelligence organization Kpler. On Monday, 21 ships went through the strait. But in the middle of July, the average number of ships passing through was 47.
How will things develop from here?

"The Houthis could actually interrupt, or at least significantly disturb, the connection between Asia and Europe," says Stephan Roll, a senior fellow with the Africa and Middle East division at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs, or SWP, in Berlin. "So first we have to wait and see how big the actual disruption to the Suez Canal will be."
Even complete control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait doesn't automatically mean control of the Suez Canal. But it does give the Houthis a further opportunity to indirectly threaten traffic.

For Egypt, this new disruption comes at a particularly unwelcome time. Houthi attacks at the end of 2023 had already disrupted business at the Suez Canal. According to the International Monetary Fund, earnings at the canal in 2024 fell by around $6 billion (€5.2 billion). Before the current security crisis, Egypt had been making between $9 billion and $10 billion from the Suez Canal annually.
More recently things had actually been improving again.
"The situation is certainly problematic compared to 2023," Roll told DW. "But it is not so clearly negative compared to the situation one, two or even three months ago."

blocks.caption: Important source of income: opening of the Suez Canal in 1869Image: akg-images/picture alliance

blocks.text: Thanks to rising oil prices and the resulting higher cost of circumnavigating Africa, shipping companies had been using the Red Sea as they travelled between Asia and Europe.

The Suez Canal's finances had recently improved. The Suez Canal Authority, which manages the passage, reported that during the 2025-2026 fiscal year, revenues had risen by 23% to $4.67 billion (€4.5 billion). Despite the various conflicts in the region, this actually represented a recovery for the Suez Canal.
Houthi offensive could change all that

There is also a second critical factor. After recent drone attacks that the Saudis blamed on Iraqi groups, Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline to the coastal city of Yanbu will be out of service for at least several weeks. Between 4 million and 5 million barrels of oil were going through the 1,200 kilometer pipeline per day as the Saudis attempted to circumnavigate the Strait of Hormuz, blocked due to the US-Iran war. This latest damage could put as much as 4% of global supply at risk, according to Reuters.

An analysis by Qatar-based think tank, the Middle East Council on Global Affairs, warns of a scenario where the Persian Gulf and Red Sea are both likely to become more precarious. The East Asia Institute, a think tank based in Korea, has also written about the dangers of dual choke points.
Neither route can be seen as an independent alternative because flows of oil and trade depend on secure connections at several points.
Certainly for Egypt, this will increase economic pressure.
What can Egypt do about this?
In geopolitical terms, there is not a lot that Egypt can do. The Houthis in Yemen have only impacted the country indirectly.
"Egypt's military capabilities are very limited," Steffen Krüger, head of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation's Cairo office, explained.

Egyptian interventions in Yemen in the 1960s are still remembered in Cairo — back then, the country sent thousands of troops to support a new government in Yemen, in a war that would eventually last years — so Egypt would prefer to exercise restraint there.
"Although Egypt formally remains a member of the Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis, its participation is largely symbolic," Krüger told DW.
And there is no doubt that Egyptian officials have noted the lack of success other countries like Saudi Arabia and the US have had in their attempts to rein in the Houthis.

"The Egyptians simply have no real alternative," argues the SWP's Roll, adding that Egypt is likely to try diplomacy first. "Basically they have to try to put a positive spin on a bad situation and somehow negotiate appropriate arrangements with the Houthis."

That may already be happening. According to London-based media outlet The New Arab on September 14, the Houthis offered to talk directy to Cairo about shipping security via the International Chamber of Shipping in London. The same publication said Egypt had rejected the offer for fear of it being seen as recognizing Houthi authority.

blocks.caption: The Strait of Hormuz has also been dangerous: This week the Panama-flagged El Gaia tanker was hit, although it is unclear by whomImage: IRIB/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: On Tuesday, Saudi Arabian leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, travelled to Cairo to try to get Egypt's support against the Houthis.
"The Egyptians are likely to wait and see," says Roll of the SWP about the next steps for Cairo.

Egypt has a difficult balancing act to perform. The country is closely allied with Saudi Arabia but is also bound to suffer economically in any further escalation between the Saudis and the Houthi group.

A decisive factor will depend on if, and how, the Houthis restrict maritime shipping, and if they go beyond vessels with Saudi Arabian ties, or whether they are just using their currenty improved military position to exert pressure on their enemies.
This story was originally published in German.

articles.title: Gun control advocacy groups push for details on weapon used in Tumbler Ridge, B.C., school shooting
articles.summary: Five gun control advocacy groups are renewing pressure on the RCMP to disclose information about the firearms used in the mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C., saying public discussion of the details…

image.caption: Community members attend a vigil on Feb. 13 for the victims of the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting. (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Five gun control advocacy groups are renewing pressure on the RCMP to disclose information about the firearms used in the mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C., saying public discussion of the details could help prevent another tragedy.
Advocates say public discussion of the details could help prevent another tragedy
The RCMP says the force cannot reveal specific information because the investigation of the February shootings at a home and school in the small community is active and ongoing.

In a Sept. 14 letter addressed to RCMP Commissioner Mike Duheme, the groups say that as a new school year begins, students, parents, teachers and communities deserve verified information that could help address failures in gun control law or its enforcement before another mass shooting happens.
"In a mass murder investigation like the one at Tumbler Ridge, operational secrecy and public accountability can coexist," the letter says.

"Police should operate on a principle of maximum transparency and minimum secrecy to maintain public trust, prevent misinformation and allow informed debates about potential policy changes to increase public safety from gun violence."

items: Teachers, students file new wave of lawsuits against OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting
'My students should be here': Tumbler Ridge teacher shares toll of deadly school shooting

blocks.text: The letter is signed by Heidi Rathjen of the group PolySeSouvient and by representatives of Angie's Angels, Canadian Doctors for Protection Against Guns, Danforth Families for Safe Communities and the Quebec Mosque.
The Feb. 10 shootings in Tumbler Ridge left nine people dead, including young assailant Jesse Van Rootselaar, who took her own life.
The Canadian Press is part of a consortium of media outlets taking legal action to obtain information about the guns used in the mass shooting and the weapons seized from the home of Van Rootselaar.

The letter from the gun control advocacy groups says no responsible person or party is asking police to release operational details, witness accounts, investigative tactics or material that could prejudice a legal process.
"But Canadians have a right to know how our gun control system worked — or failed to work — when multiple children are shot and killed in a matter of minutes," the letter reads.

The groups seek details about the guns involved in the killings, including make, model, type, classification and legal status, along with relevant information about magazines, prohibited devices, ammunition or accessories.

items: 'Red flag' gun laws under scrutiny after Tumbler Ridge, B.C., shooting
What we know — and don't — about the guns used in the Tumbler Ridge, B.C., shooting

blocks.text: In the event disclosure must still be delayed, the groups say they want a clear explanation of the type of information being withheld and a sense of when the RCMP will be able to provide an update.
Copies of the letter were sent to several politicians, including Prime Minister Mark Carney, Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree and British Columbia Premier David Eby.
Teachers, students file 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting
RCMP Staff Sgt. Kris Clark, an RCMP spokesperson, said in a statement that because the police probe remains active, "we cannot discuss any specific details or investigative actions."
Clark said the B.C. RCMP remains committed to "providing answers where and when we can, and we appreciate the public’s patience as verified, official information becomes available."
Clark pointed to the RCMP's July 7 statement on the shootings, which said firearms assessments were being completed.
"This continues to be a criminal investigation, in which we have not eliminated the possibility that charges could be laid," the July statement said.

"It is important to understand that the absence of publicly disclosed details does not mean investigators do not have that information. Rather, we must protect the integrity of the ongoing investigation, particularly with potential future prosecution in mind."

articles.title: ICC orders Rodrigo Duterte’s continued detention
articles.summary: 'The Chamber therefore finds no notable change in circumstances that warrant the release of the Accused, with or without conditions,' says the order issued by the ICC Trial Chamber III

blocks.text: DUTERTE. Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte appears before the International Criminal Court, as the court hears arguments regarding Duterte's health and ability to stand trial, while he faces murder charges related to his war on drugs, in The Hague, Netherlands, on September 16 2026.
Piroschka van de Wouw/Pool via Reuters
'The Chamber therefore finds no notable change in circumstances that warrant the release of the Accused, with or without conditions,' says the order issued by the ICC Trial Chamber III
MANILA, Philippines – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III ordered the continued detention of former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte at The Hague, Netherlands.

“The Chamber therefore finds no notable change in circumstances that warrant the release of the Accused, with or without conditions. For these reasons, the chamber hereby decides that the accused shall continue to be detained,” said the chamber’s decision on Wednesday, September 16.
In May, the chamber said Duterte is still not qualified to avail himself of temporary liberty, ruling that the former president shall continue to be detained.

At the ICC, chambers conduct a yearly review to check if detention is still warranted for an accused. Specifically, the judges will check for changed circumstances that would warrant temporary liberty for detained suspects.
After the May resolution, the chamber reviewed Duterte’s continued detention again.
According to the trial chamber, it found that there’s a likelihood that Duterte would “abscond,” “obstruct,” or “endanger” the court proceedings.

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the court explained.

The court is also assessing Duterte’s fitness for trial. But even though the results of this assessment are still pending, the “panel’s reports do not contain any information that warrants a modification of the accused’s detention,” the court said.

Under the Rome Statute, which created the ICC, a suspect cannot be released if they present risk factors, which include the danger of fleeing, obstructing justice by intimidating witnesses, or recommitting the same alleged crimes.

blocks.caption: Rodrigo Duterte attends ICC hearing in person for the first time

blocks.text: “Accordingly, the Chamber finds that the risks under Article 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) have increased and, in respect of the risks outlined in Article 58(1)(b)(iii), sees no change in circumstances,” the court explained.

The chamber held the third status conference on Duterte’s case on Wednesday, where the parties discussed the possible evidence for the upcoming November 30 trial. Duterte appeared during the hearing, marking his first personal appearance before the court since his arrest in March 2025. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained - ICC trial chamber
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

blocks.text: Filtered By: Topstories
News
Published September 16, 2026 9:46pm

Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appears before the International Criminal Court, as the court hears arguments regarding Duterte's health and ability to stand trial, while he faces murder charges related to his war on drugs, in The Hague, Netherlands, September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw/Pool
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.
The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Saudis pound Yemen as Houthis solidify gains in new Middle East war front
articles.summary: Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen, the Houthis said on Wednesday, as the Iran-backed fighters solidified their gains after a lightning advance that has extended Tehran's reach in the Middle East war and…

image.caption: Men ride in the back of a pickup truck during a mass funeral procession for Houthi officers and other military personnel in Sanaa, Yemen, on Wednesday. (The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World

Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen, the Houthis said on Wednesday, as the Iran-backed fighters solidified their gains after a lightning advance that has extended Tehran's reach in the Middle East war and further disrupted global oil supplies.
Houthis recently swept through Yemeni towns along the Red Sea coast, seized islands

Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen and Houthi fighters launched drones and missiles at Saudi cities, the Iran-backed movement said Wednesday, after a lightning advance that has extended Tehran's reach in the Middle East war.

In a sign of the worsening conflict in a new theatre, the United States tightened its travel warning for Saudi Arabia, banning government employees from travelling within 32 kilometres of the Yemen border.

The Houthis, who since last week have swept through Yemeni towns along the Red Sea coast and seized islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, released battlefield video overnight of fighters seizing armoured vehicles from Saudi-backed forces. Warplanes flew overhead and huge explosions billowed into the sky from desert dunes, the video showed.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had launched fresh drone and missile strikes on the major Saudi Red Sea oil port of Yanbu, and at a southern Saudi airbase at Khamis Mushait. He did not say when the strikes had taken place.
Both cities were among a wide range of locations where Saudi Arabia announced alerts on Tuesday, although there were no similar announcements on Wednesday.
Saudi officials and oil company Aramco did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.
Earlier, Saree said the Houthis had also shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. No immediate evidence was presented of that incident.
Houthi rebel control expands over key oil shipping lane

Saree said the Saudis had carried out as many as 450 airstrikes on Yemen this week. Officials in the Saudi-backed government that controls southern Yemen have acknowledged that their forces and those of Saudi Arabia were conducting airstrikes on Houthi positions, though Riyadh itself has not confirmed them.

The Houthis have fired repeatedly into Saudi Arabia over the past week, causing alarms over cities in the south and west. An attack blamed on Iran-aligned fighters in Iraq last week also knocked out Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the main route used to divert oil exports from the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

Riyadh said its air defences had shot down a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, an attack it said crossed a "red line" of threatening shrines sacred to all Muslims.
Houthi spokesperson Saree denied the group had targeted Mecca, and said the Saudi reports were a setup for propaganda purposes.

Sources told Reuters that U.S. officials had held a meeting with the Houthis over the weekend in Oman, at which the group said it had no intention of attacking American vessels and was committed to a ceasefire reached with the U.S. last year.
Danger of global energy supply shortage worsening

The extension of the war into Yemen threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused by the six-month-old U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The price of Brent crude hovered around $108 US a barrel on Wednesday, close to its highest level since May. The politically sensitive average retail price of diesel fuel in the United States hit another all-time high above $6.30 US a gallon for the first time.

Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline could cut off as much as four per cent of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume, but U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days.

items: Houthis attack more Saudi targets as regional talks with Iran postponed
Houthis seize strategic island, Saudis close pipeline as fighting escalates

blocks.text: Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quietened under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and fired at southern areas in the kingdom. Violence has intensified sharply this month when the militant group pushed back forces aligned with the Saudi-backed internationally recognized Yemeni government.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned U.S. President Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid.
The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in 2025, but halted that campaign after reaching what Trump described as a ceasefire that would halt attacks on ships.

Trump now faces a dilemma of whether to stand by and risk the Houthi advance worsening the global energy crisis, or provide more direct military support to the Saudis and risk extending the costly U.S. intervention to another theatre.

articles.title: Witness: Marcoleta's donors provided funds for his 2025 Senate campaign
articles.summary: The three individuals who donated money to then Sagip party-list Rep. Rodante Marcoleta did so to support his possible 2025 Senate candidacy, a witness from the Office of the Ombudsman told the…

blocks.text: Published September 16, 2026 9:31pm

The three individuals who donated money to then Sagip party-list Rep. Rodante Marcoleta did so to support his possible 2025 Senate candidacy, a witness from the Office of the Ombudsman told the anti-graft court.

Field Investigation Bureau Director Maria Melinda Mananghaya-Henson, citing the Deed of Donation executed by Michael Defensor, Joseph Varias Espiritu and Aristotle Baluyut Viray, made the testimony before the Sandiganbayan Third Division during the hearing on the pending bail petition of Marcoleta.

The Deed of Donation stated that they gave the money to Marcoleta “for and in consideration of my support for the possible candidacy of Donee (Marcoleta) in the May 12, 2025 elections” and that all three Deed of Donation.

Defensor, Espiritu and Viray were all Marcoleta’s co-accused in the P75 million plunder case over Marcoleta’s alleged failure to declare the said P75 million under his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE).
During the same hearing, the video of Marcoleta saying that he willfully refused to declare the P75 million campaign donation he received from his donors was played before the anti-graft court.

“Kapag naglagay ako ng figure sa contribution, mapipilitan ako mag-disclose ng pangalan nila dahil mayroon kaakibat na kung tawagin ay deed of acceptance of donation. Papaano iyon? Sabi niya, binigay ko nga sa iyo ‘yan. Ituring mo na lang na utang. Dahil sa hindi ko pwedeng isiwalat ang kanilang identity, kaya sinabi ko, zero in contribution,” Marcoleta said in the video of his television show.

(If I put a figure on their contribution, I would be forced to drop their names due to deed of acceptance of donation. How do I deal with it then? I was told that the money given to me can be treated as a loan. And since I cannot disclose their identity, I stated zero contribution.)
Nelson Lubao, who interviewed Marcoleta during the said November 8, 2025 television episode on Net 25, earlier asked the court to be excused as a witness for the prosecution.

Ahead of Henson’s testimony, prosecution witness Atty. Victoria Kadeja Besinio of the Commission on Elections (Comelec) Political Finance and Affairs Department also testified that Marcoleta, in his position paper submitted to the poll body, said the P75 million formed part of his personal funds.
On Wednesday, the Office of the Ombudsman assured the public that "there is very strong evidence on record that warranted the filing of the case" against Marcoleta and his co-accused. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Federal authorities cancel Edmonton mom's removal from Canada hours before she boards plane
articles.summary: In an email, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada said Halima Abdi’s application for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds passed eligibility requirements on Sept. 9.

image.caption: An undated file photo of Halima Abdi and her youngest son after learning a previous removal had been cancelled. (Travis McEwan/CBC News)

blocks.text: Edmonton
In an email, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada said Halima Abdi’s application for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds passed eligibility requirements on Sept. 9.
CBSA says it stayed removal order pending outcome of woman’s application for permanent residence

Calling while being detained by officials near Edmonton's airport earlier this month, Halima Abdi tried to comfort her three little boys huddled in the back seat of her sister’s vehicle outside a Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) office.

Earlier that day, Sept. 4, authorities unexpectedly detained Abdi, who went into the CBSA building in downtown Edmonton for her weekly check-in. After a decade-long battle to stay in Canada, Abdi's removal was just six days away.
"Why did you leave us, Mommy?,” her eldest — seven years old — asked, putting a protective arm around his sibling.
"Mommy, come back," her youngest pleaded.
What unfolded over the next 72 hours, according to Abdi, was nothing short of a miracle.
On the same day she was supposed to fly back to Kenya, immigration authorities approved — in principle — Abdi's application for permanent residency on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
In an interview with CBC News on Tuesday, Abdi tried to find the words to thank dozens of her supporters who have stood by her for nearly a decade.
“I don't know how to express my gratitude to everybody," she said. "I will just pray for them.”

items: Motherhood issue: Federal gov't urged to halt deportations that separate moms from children

blocks.text: Abdi's bid to start a new life in Canada began in February 2017 when she flew from Kenya to the United States and walked across the northern border.
Canadian immigration authorities at the time rejected Abdi’s claim that she was a target in Kenya because of her Somali ethnicity.
Two unpalatable options remained: surrender her children to be raised by the Alberta government, or bring them with her to Kenya.

Supporters gathered in protest outside of the downtown Edmonton CBSA building on Sept. 4 as Abdi's lawyer and advocates wrote emails to the federal public safety minister. More than 1,000 people signed a petition asking immigration authorities to reconsider.

In the meantime, officials flew Abdi to a detention centre in B.C. and then back to Edmonton. She was finally released from custody on Sept. 10 at Edmonton International Airport and into the arms of relieved family members.

In an email to CBC News, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) said Abdi’s August 2024 application for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds passed the eligibility requirements on Sept. 9.

The CBSA said it received confirmation from the IRCC on Sept. 10 and stayed the removal order pending the outcome of her application for permanent residence, which involves further medical and security checks.
Now, as Abdi cherishes the daily moments with her kids, she is also daring to dream about what a future career in Canada might look like, either in policing, the military or in medicine.
“When I think back, I'm like, ‘Girl, you're so strong. If this did not break you, nothing's going to break you,'” Abdi said.

articles.title: Iran: Activists sound alarm as regime seizes Baha'i assets
articles.summary: Rights groups warn Iran is increasingly confiscating assets from government critics and members of the country's Baha'i faith, but also actors, athletes, and journalists living abroad.

image.caption: Activists report Iran's security forces taking gold, electronics, tools, wedding rings, and even children's toys during recent home raidsImage: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: As Washington attempts to intensify economic pressure on Iran, ordinary Iranians face mounting financial distress.

Rights groups say Iranian authorities are increasingly using asset seizures against religious minorities, dissidents and government critics, adding a new layer of economic pressure for people already struggling with soaring living costs.
Members of Iran's Baha'i religious minority seem to be bearing the brunt of the crackdown.

The faith, which originated in 19th-century Persia — now Iran — is not officially recognized by the Islamic Republic. Unlike Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians, Baha'is are not protected under Article 13 of Iran's constitution, leaving them vulnerable to longstanding discrimination and persecution.
Baha'is portrayed as 'spies' for Israel
The US-based Human Rights Activists in Iran (HRANA) reported "a wave of arrests, searches of homes and businesses, and seizures of property belonging to Baha'i citizens" at the end of August.

Amnesty International said persecution of the Baha'i community has intensified since the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025, citing what it described as "a coordinated state campaign of incitement to hostility, violence, discrimination and disinformation falsely accusing Baha'is as spies and collaborators for Israel."

blocks.caption: Bahai activist Padideh Sabeti says Tehran's 'discriminatory practices' deprive Baha'is of the ability to earn a livingImage: privat

blocks.text: "Under current conditions, all people in Iran are facing economic hardship and extremely difficult living conditions, barely putting food on the table for their families," says Padideh Sabeti, spokesperson for the International Baha'i Community.
However, Baha'is suffer even more from the country's economic situation, "as the government's discriminatory practices deprive them of the ability to earn a living," she added.
Sabeti adds that the judiciary uses poverty as leverage, demanding exorbitant bail "which is sometimes equivalent to a hundred years' wages for an average citizen."
Regime goes after prominent critics

The apparatus of repression does not only target religious minorities. The government has announced judiciary orders identifying and seizing assets belonging to over 400 individuals living abroad who authorities described as "supporters of the enemy," including actors, athletes, and overseas journalists.

Domestically, Sadegh Saedinia, manager of the "Saedinia" chain of cafes, received a 12-year prison sentence, a two-year operating ban, and total asset confiscation for posting content related to anti-government protests in Qom, a conservative city considered sacred to Shiites.
The growing number of confiscations has led some observers to ask whether property seizures are also aimed at filling state coffers at a time of economic strain.

blocks.caption: The resources gained through seizures are 'very, very insignificant' compared with Iran's massive budget deficitImage: Privat

blocks.text: The economics of confiscation

Arezoo Karimi, a London-based economic analyst, says the financial impact is likely to be limited. The resources gained through seizures are "very, very insignificant" compared with Iran's massive budget deficit, she said.
According to Karimi, confiscated properties are often auctioned off below market value to individuals with political connections.
Sajjad Khodakarami, a Paris-based journalist, says targeting diaspora dissidents sends a clear psychological warning.
"This tool — which the Islamic Republic previously tested on a segment of society — is now being deployed on a broader scale against its opponents," Khodakarami said.

"Today, this instrument of repression targets not only parts of the Baha'i community, but also various strata of society, including journalists, social and human rights activists, and artists who oppose the ruling political establishment," he added.
"When the Islamic Republic targets the assets of hundreds of people, it sends them a message: Even when you are beyond our physical reach, we will continue to apply pressure on you from all sides."
Toys and wedding rings seized by law enforcement
International human rights monitors reported security forces taking gold, electronics, work tools, wedding rings, and children's toys during recent home raids.
Khodakarami views the confiscation of everyday household items as a dark indicator of the regime's trajectory.

"When government agents stoop so low as to confiscate a couple's wedding rings or a child's toys, it is a sign of barbarism," said Khodakarami. "Moreover, this behavior is not merely a message to the Baha'i community, but a broader warning to all dissidents."

blocks.caption: Khodakarami says post-protest Iran is witnessing 'both the securitization of the economy and the economization of repression'Image: Privat

blocks.text: Khodakarami argues that the government is placing a growing share of the economic burden on ordinary citizens rather than on powerful state institutions.
"As the regime's resources shrink, it tightens the screw on the people's livelihoods," Khodakarami said.
Can Iran avoid hyperinflation?

According to Karimi, the government is relying on money printing and subsidy rollbacks to compensate for declining foreign currency revenues. The analyst warns that current fiscal policies risk pushing the country into galloping inflation.
"On one hand, banks are creating money, while on the other, production is effectively paralyzed," said Karimi.

"If we continue down this path at the current pace, I foresee a day when hyperinflation hits Iran — a day when people pay one fare to commute to work in the morning, but have to pay up to double that for the ride back home, just like what we witnessed in Venezuela and Zimbabwe."

While seizing personal assets may serve as a tool of intimidation and generate limited funds for the security apparatus, analysts say it cannot fix Iran's underlying economic problems and is unlikely to ease the financial pressures facing ordinary Iranians.

articles.title: Small plane makes emergency landing on highway east of Edmonton
articles.summary: Strathcona County RCMP say a Cessna 172 touched down on Highway 21 with two people on board.

image.caption: Alberta RCMP say a small plane made an emergency landing on a highway east of Edmonton early Wednesday. The Cessna 172 was later pulled off the highway and onto the shoulder of a nearby range road. (David Bajer/CBC)

blocks.text: Edmonton
Strathcona County RCMP say a Cessna 172 touched down on Highway 21 with two people on board.
No injuries reported as Cessna 172 touches down with 2 people on board
Alberta RCMP say a small plane was forced to make an emergency landing on a highway east of Edmonton early Wednesday.
RCMP say a Cessna 172 plane, with two people on board, touched down on Highway 21 in Strathcona County and came to rest in the southbound lanes between Highway 16 and Baseline Road.
Police say the call came in around 1:30 a.m. and officers were dispatched to the scene.
There were no reports of other injuries or of any collisions between the aircraft and vehicles on the highway, RCMP said.
In an interview Wednesday, RCMP Const. Sandra Geiger said the occupants of the plane, a pilot and a passenger, were not injured.
It's unclear if any vehicles were on the highway when the plane touched down, she said.
"When the initial call out came in, there was no vehicles involved, which is a rather good thing," she said.
"I think part of that might have been the time of day in terms of the involvement. But I don't know if there was any vehicles that had to avoid the area."
Alberta RCMP remained at the scene throughout the morning and the highway was closed for hours.
As of 7:30, the highway had been reopened to traffic after the plane was moved east off the highway and pushed onto the shoulder of a nearby range road.
The four-seat, single-engine, fixed wing aircraft — painted red and white — showed no apparent signs of damage.
RCMP say the Transportation Safety Board (TSB) has been alerted to the incident and is expected to lead the investigation.
In a statement to CBC News Wednesday, officials with the TSB said the aircraft lost engine power and was unable to maintain flight.
The forced landing on the highway happened around 1:15 a.m., resulting in no damage to the aircraft and no injury to the pilot or passenger.
The agency said it has no plans to deploy investigators to the scene but will continue to collect information and assess the circumstances of the forced landing.

articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.summary:
Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled…

blocks.text: Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

Born in Chile in 1941, Guzmán initially worked in advertising before studying film, first in Chile and then in Madrid. On his return to Chile, Guzmán responded to the febrile political atmosphere after Allende’s election in 1970, eventually completing the mammoth Battle of Chile documentary that chronicled Pinochet’s ultimately successful attempt to overthrow Allende, resulting in the latter’s suicide. Guzmán did not shrink from the brutality of the period, even including footage shot by camera operator Leonardo Henrichsen as he is shot dead by the soldier he is filming.

blocks.caption: A still from The Battle of Chile. Photograph: Collection Christophel/Alamy

blocks.text: Guzmán was helped in the endeavour by French film-maker Chris Marker, who supplied film stock and connections that proved vital to make the film. Guzmán himself was arrested but eventually released, but the film’s cinematographer Jorge Müller was not so lucky – along with his girlfriend Carmen Bueno, he was arrested, tortured and “disappeared” in 1974.

Guzmán completed The Battle of Chile outside the country, releasing each of its three parts – The Insurrection of the Bourgeoisie (1975), The Coup d’État (1976) and Popular Power (1979) – through the rest of the 70s. Described by the Guardian as “an outstandingly photographed example of a newsreel film that captures the drama and volatility of the period”, it has continued to attract acclaim since then. Guzmán revisited the film in the mid-90s with Chile, Obstinate Memory, in which he returned to the country after a quarter-century of exile. In 2001 he completed The Pinochet Case, after the Chilean former dictator was arrested in London in 1998.

The director moved on to more metaphysical subjects with a trilogy of films starting in 2010: Nostalgia for the Light, The Pearl Button and The Cordillera of Dreams. They sought to explore Chile’s traumatic past by absorbing the country’s magnificent natural landscapes. articles.title: PDEA says P500-million confidential funds for anti-drugs ops
articles.summary: A member of the House of Representatives on Wednesday questioned the P500 million in confidential funds sought by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) for 2027.

blocks.text: Published September 16, 2026 8:41pm

A member of the House of Representatives on Wednesday questioned the P500 million in confidential funds sought by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) during the plenary interpellations for PDEA's proposed P4.4-billion budget for 2027.

In response to Philreca Party-list Representative Presley de Jesus' question about the proposed allocation, budget sponsor Representative Marcy Teodoro said the PDEA has been receiving P500 million in confidential funds since 2025, and that this was for anti-drug operations.

"High-impact operations and disruptions of major organizations. The NEP reports that in 2025, 1,471 of 1,991 drug-related information na reports are acted upon or 73.88% resulted in anti-drug operations. Admittedly, not 100% of the drug-related information are acted favorably," said Teodoro, who is also vice chairperson of the House Committee on Appropriations.
Teodoro, however, stated that the PDEA exceeded its target in going after drug suspects.

"In terms of percentage decrease in drug personalities, the target actually is 10% as set forth in this year’s budget. We were able to arrest 173 personalities totaling to or accounting for 10.18% of the target. So we exceeded a bit from the target," he said.

"In terms of high-value targets arrested, our target, as I have mentioned earlier, is 60% of the total arrests. And we were able to have an arrest of 2,368 out of 2,819 on the list. That is 84% accomplishment. And the number of high-impact operations conducted, as I have mentioned in my sponsorship speech, the 500 operations that we targeted this year, we already exceeded that in the number of 696 operations, as we speak now," he added.
Teodoro, who also sponsored the budget for the Dangerous Drugs Board for 2027 amounting to P526.54 million, also reported a decrease in the number of drug users in the country.
Teodoro, citing the 2023 National Household Survey, said that from 2019 when 1,675,000 individuals used illegal drugs, the number dropped to 1,479,000 in 2023.
"That decline is encouraging pero hindi ibig sabihin na puwede na tayong maging kampante. Mahigit isang milyong Pilipino pa rin yan," Teodoro emphasized.
(It doesn't mean we can become complacent. That's still more than one million Filipinos.)

"The task is broader than simply counting facilities. The value of DDB's coordinating role is to help government understand what kind if help is needed, where it is needed, and how people can actually reach it," he said.
The DDB is also responsible for coming out with the Philippine Anti Drugs Strategy (PADS) which is expected to be approved within the year.

"Kasulukuyan po, yung PADS natin ay nire-review. Nasa Presidential Management Staff ito for review and consideration at naghihintay tayo ng enhanced PADS based on the executive order dahil nagbago ang panahon at problema," Teodoro said.
(Currently, PADS is under review by the Presidential Management Staff and we are waiting for the enhanced PADS based on the executive order because the climate and the problems change.)

"Tulad ngayon, ang isang strategy pong kailangan ay hindi na ito dapat street-level drugs na lamang o kaya individual basis kundi ito ay naging transnational na yung [One important strategy is that it should not just be at the level of street-level drugs or in an individual bses, but on transnational shipments] shipment [of] drugs coming [from] outside of the country going into and being distributed. There's an observation that it's already a syndicate operating the drug distribution of illegal drugs. Somebody will finance it. And there will be in charge, different organizations and individuals, in the selling and distribution," he added. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Party leaders to negotiate coalition in BARMM Parliament
articles.summary: Right now, 'it is the Bangsamoro Federalist Party as the single biggest party that will have the first opportunity to form a government,' says Member of Parliament-elect Ishak Mastura

blocks.text: ELECTIONS. Voters wait outside the precinct during the first parliamentary elections of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao in Pahamuddin, Cotabato, on September 14, 2026.
Manman Dejeto/Reuters
Right now, 'it is the Bangsamoro Federalist Party as the single biggest party that will have the first opportunity to form a government,' says Member of Parliament-elect Ishak Mastura

items: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is facing a hung parliament after the elections on September 14, with the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) holding 31 seats and the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) holding 30 seats.
Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua emphasized the need for coalition-building among parties to establish a government, with discussions already initiated with other political groups.
The elected parliament will assume office on October 30, and a majority of at least 41 seats is required to influence the selection of the chief minister.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
COTABATO CITY, Philippines – After the historic polls on Monday, September 14, the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is now facing a hung parliament.
BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua said a coalition with other parties is an “unavoidable situation” to establish a government.

“I’ve already called up the three governors, members of the [Bangsamoro Federalist Party], to come and discuss what we call the coalition or to establish a government,” Macacua told reporters on Tuesday, September 15.

Macacua is president of the leading regional political party Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), which has a total of 31 seats. The United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), led by Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) Chairman Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, got 30 seats.

“We need really to coalesce with parties that are likewise advocating similar platforms of government,” Mohagher Iqbal, MILF vice chairman and Bangsamoro Member of Parliament-elect, told media on Wednesday, September 16.

The Macacua-led BFP and Murad-led UBJP would have to establish alliances with the BARMM Grand Coalition (BGC), which managed to get a total of 15 seats, if their goal is to grab a greater hold of the Bangsamoro Parliament.

The BGC is composed of the Bangsamoro Peoples Party, Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo, and Al-Ittihad-Ungaya sa Kawagib Nu Bangsamoro. The coalition is led by Abdulrahman Rubbil Sangki Mangudadatu, alongside political dynasties such as the Adiong clan.

The elected parliament will assume office on October 30 and eventually choose Bangsamoro’s chief minister. A majority of at least 41 seats guarantees that the party with the highest number of members of parliament would have the most influence on who gets to take the seat as chief minister.
According to BGC nominee and Member of Parliament-elect Amir Mawallil, leadership in the coalition has yet to meet to discuss possible alliances with either the BFP or UBJP.
It is also possible that all three parties coalesce, depending on where the talks lead, said Ishak Mastura, Member of Parliament-elect for Maguindanao del Norte 5th District.
“But right now, it is the BFP as the single biggest party that will have the first opportunity to form a government,” Mastura told Rappler.

blocks.caption: Here are the results of 2026 BARMM parliamentary elections

blocks.text: Tensions among supporters of different parties diffused the next day, when results were being transmitted and winners proclaimed. Will tensions affect negotiations to form a government?

“I think the tension will eventually die down in due time,” Mastura said. “But right now, of course, people are still suffering from the pangs of the campaign. And it was a hard campaign. It was hard fought.”

Voter turnout for the polls was over 84%, according to the Commission on Elections. Authorities have said the elections have been generally peaceful and safe despite eruptions of violence in parts of the region. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: ROOKIE. Kieffer Alas in action for the Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP Season 89 men's basketball tournament.
UAAP
Rookie guard Kieffer Alas shows the way for Ateneo in its blowout of UE, which comes exactly 100 days since Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili died from drowning during the Blue Eagles' team building

items: The Ateneo Blue Eagles began the UAAP Season 89 with a dominant 101-74 victory over the UE Red Warriors, inspired by the memory of teammates Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili.
Rookie Kieffer Alas led the team with 24 points in his debut, while the team dedicated the game to the families of the deceased players present at the match.
Ateneo aims for a strong season after struggling in previous years, with assistant coach RJ Jazul noting the players' resilience despite their emotional challenges.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – With Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili in mind, the Ateneo Blue Eagles opened the new UAAP season with aplomb.
The Blue Eagles coasted to rousing 101-74 win over the UE Red Warriors to start their campaign in the Season 89 men’s basketball tournament at the Mall of Asia Arena on Wednesday, September 16.

Rookie Kieffer Alas turned in a UAAP seniors debut to remember, firing 24 points with 4 rebounds in just 20 minutes of action to show the way in the victory which came exactly 100 days since Baterbonia and Adili died from drowning during a team building in Dipaculao, Aurora, on June 8.
“I feel like this was just an introduction to Ateneo,” said Alas. “After everything that happened, everyone counted us out. So I hope that slowly, we can bring ourselves where we want to be.
Ateneo raced to a 25-16 lead at the end of the opening quarter and cruised the rest of the way as it leaned on the trio of Alas, Jared Bahay, and Grayson Rogers.

Bahay finished with 17 points, 2 rebounds, and 2 assists, while Rogers supplied 12 points, 2 assists, and 2 steals in the blowout which saw the Blue Eagles mount a lead as big as 38 points in the fourth period, 93-55.
It was a statement win for Ateneo, which drew inspiration from the presence of Adili’s parents, Elias and Ifeoma.
Elias and Ifeoma Adili are in the Philippines to watch Ateneo’s first two games of the season.

“The whole season, we dedicate it to Divine and Rene. But for this game, since you’re here, we dedicate it to you guys,” Bahay recalled from his conversation with the Adilis. “I made sure my teammates heard what I said so they know that we cannot lose because they’re there.”
Andrew Bongo also made his presence felt for the Blue Eagles with 9 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 blocks, Jay-M Leal chipped in 6 points and 9 rebounds, while Shawn Tuano added 6 points and 5 rebounds.

For Ateneo assistant coach RJ Jazul, the victory is a step in the right direction for the Blue Eagles, who are eyeing a return to the Final Four after failing to reach the semifinals in the last two seasons.
“The players’ emotional baggage will always be there, but still, they keep on grinding every day through hard practices. They’re all going hard,” said Jazul.

Toper Lagat finished with 15 points, while JM Edoukou put up 14 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 steals for the Red Warriors, who absorbed their 21st consecutive UAAP defeat, their losing streak dating back to Season 87. – Rappler.com

articles.title: US accuses Russia of trying to kill Ukrainian allies overseas
articles.summary: The FBI says five men "conspired to intimidate, threaten, or murder people on US soil and around the world".

blocks.text: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has accused Russia of plotting to murder Ukrainian allies in the US and Europe.

In a statement on Tuesday, the DoJ charged five men allegedly connected to the Russian Intelligence Services (RIS). The men are accused of paying, or trying to pay, people in the US and overseas to target those "aligned, or perceived to be aligned, with Ukraine".
"It is our job to stop America's adversaries from unleashing violence and terror on American soil," Attorney General Todd Blanche. All those accused remain at large.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Wednesday Moscow will not comment until it hears or sees "any credible evidence" or "tangible facts".
It is not clear if the five accused are in the United States, or in a different location.
Washington has charged all five men with participating in a conspiracy to finance terrorism, which carries a maximum 20-year prison sentence.
Three of the defendants are "high-ranking members of the RIS network", the DoJ said.

Among them are Russian father and son Yuri Khrameev, 63, and Kirill Khrameev, 27. Khrameev senior was a colonel in the Russian intelligence services and his son is an officer in the Federal Security Service of Russia (FSB).

The third high-ranking suspect is Oemis Romagoza Durruthy, a 35-year-old Cuban national who the US describe as "an influential member of the Cuban diaspora living in Russia who has coordinated attacks for the RIS network".
Yaidel Delgado Suarez, 35, and Angel Eduardo Castro, 22, are the other two defendants.
The pair are accused of recruiting or attempting to recruit US-based individuals to "surveil and attempt to murder a prominent US-based Russian dissident".
The FBI's James Barnacle said the group "conspired to intimidate, threaten, or murder people on US soil and around the world".
One of the incidents is as recent as this summer. The DoJ described how the RIS network was able to recruit someone in the US to surveil and eventually murder a Russian dissident in the US.

Suarez allegedly sent the recruit to two locations linked to the victim with "explicit instructions on how to conduct surveillance". In exchange, the recruit was offered between $1,000 (£743) and $1,500.
Suarez and Castro are said to have offered an additional $40,000 if the US resident could "eliminate" the dissident.

The DoJ said the RIS recruit did not go through with it, which led Suarez to try and recruit "multiple other individuals within the United States". He allegedly offered "substantial sums of money to carry out the targeting of US based victims".
The release by the DoJ goes on to list other instances in which the accused allegedly tried to recruit others to kill those who were a perceived threat to Russia.

It said that in 2025, Khrameev junior allegedly recruited a US citizen to surveil and murder someone in Lithuania who was "telling lies about Russia". The release quotes Khrameev as saying the purpose was to target "all the countries that are helping Ukraine".
His father, Khrameev senior, is said to have offered the recruit $25,000 to kill the individual in Lithuania for "spreading dirt about my country" and "distorting history".

Khrameev senior, Suarez and Castro are the only ones also charged with "participating in a conspiracy to commit murder for hire". If found guilty, this charge carries a maximum 10-year prison sentence.
It is not the first time authorities thwart threats of this kind.
Last month, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities had detained an individual allegedly working for the Kremlin and who was plotting to murder an American-Ukrainian citizen in Warsaw.

Tusk told reporters the American-Ukrainian citizen "was uncomfortable for the Putin regime", adding: "We have to accept the assumption that the Putin regime will try to eliminate people who are inconvenient for various reasons."
In 2024, German authorities were reportedly warned by US intelligence of a Russian plot to kill Armin Papperger, the head of Germany's biggest arms company Rheinmetall.
Moscow dismissed the accusation at the time, with Kremlin spokesman Peskov saying: "It's all presented in the style of another fake story, so such reports cannot be taken seriously."
The fresh accusations from the DoJ come at a time of closer relations between Moscow and Washington following US President Donald Trump's return to the White House in 2025.
A few weeks ago, the head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) visited Moscow for talks with figures from Russia's intelligence services - an unconventional move that led to speculation.
The Kremlin confirmed that talks between John Ratcliffe and the intelligence services had taken place. President Trump did not say what was discussed but described the meeting as "semi-routine".

articles.title: Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
articles.summary: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

image.caption: A petrol station approximately 800 meters (874 yards) from the Polish-Ukrainian border was hit by a drone early on Sunday morningImage: Sylwester Uchanski/REUTERS

blocks.text: Russia's war against Ukraine is moving ever closer to the border with Poland.

After a drone attack by Russia destroyed a gas station and the locomotive of a passenger train near the Dorohusk-Yahodyn border crossing between Poland and Ukraine early Sunday, Warsaw has demonstrated its determination in the face of the immediate threat.

"Border crossings in Poland — as has previously been the case in Moldova and Romania — are being targeted in an attempt to discourage people and deter countries from supporting Ukraine," Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz told the private broadcaster TVN on Monday.
"Support for Ukraine is part of Poland's reason of state," Kosiniak-Kamysz said. He added that Poland's own security situation would be worsened should Ukraine lose the war.
Poland prepares response

Early on Monday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk met with the ministers responsible for Poland's security. Senior military commanders also attended the meeting. "We discussed further measures to strengthen the security of our borders," Tusk subsequently wrote on the social media platform X.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski provided more details.

"Poland will provide a nonprovocative but serious response to Russia's escalation, such as the attack on the train in Ukraine near the Polish border, one that will strengthen security," Poland's top diplomat told TVN Monday evening.

blocks.caption: This truck was destroyed in a Russian drone attack near the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing on the Poland-Ukraine borderImage: Sylwester Uchanski/REUTERS

blocks.text: On Sunday, Tusk spoke of an "escalation of activities" by Russia. The prime minister also announced that he would discuss the incident with Poland's allies in Europe.
"There is no doubt that we, if necessary, must be prepared, together with them, to deliver a coordinated response," Tusk said after a special session of the Government Centre for Security.
Drone attack on Kyiv-Warsaw train

Russian drones attacked a passenger train on the Kyiv-Warsaw line just short of the Polish border on Sunday morning. The train's locomotive was destroyed in the attack. All passengers and crew were evacuated in time.
Two special trains carrying high-profile participants returning from a security conference in Kyiv were nearby at almost the same time as the attack.

Among those on board were former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt, former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson, former Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin, former Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski and Günter Sautter, foreign and security policy adviser to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Polish political scientist Katarzyna Piskorska, who has organized the Warsaw Security Forum in the Polish capital for years, was also on the train.

"Our train was stopped beforehand, and the passengers were evacuated," she told TVN. "The situation was very tense, but everyone remained calm. We were given an evacuation plan and knew exactly what to do."
Russia turns to jet-powered drones to wear Kyiv down
"The Russians wanted to intimidate us, but they achieved the opposite: The participants affected by this incident are determined to step up their support for the country that was attacked," she said.

Piskorska said the mood in Ukraine was "worse than at any time since the start of the war." She pointed to a new generation of drones equipped with jet engines that can reach their targets much faster.
Support for Ukraine slipping in Poland

Despite numerous acts of sabotage assumed to have be carried out by Russian agents and incidents involving Russian missiles and drones, Poland's government has remained firm in its commitment to supporting Ukraine.
Foreign Minister Sikorski has even called for support for Ukraine to be doubled, arguing that doing so is in Poland's own security interest.
But the government in Warsaw also has to consider the shift in Polish public opinion.

In a survey conducted in mid-July, 52% of respondents said they were in favor of continued military aid for Kyiv; 45% opposed it. These figures stood at 77.5% and 18.3%, respectively, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

"Russia has won the propaganda war in Poland," Piskorska said. "It is absurd that we are taking the side of the aggressor and claiming that this is not our war," she said, appealing to fellow Poles to "finally wake up."
Defense Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz has also expressed concern about what he described as a "radical shift in sentiment."

blocks.caption: Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski has called for support for Ukraine to be doubled, arguing that this is in the interest of Polish security Image: Christoph Soeder/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "In the past, there was consensus on this issue. Today, we are seeing great skepticism toward Ukraine," Kosiniak-Kamysz said. "There are forces in Poland that are spreading Russian propaganda," he added.
Polish media sound alarm
The Polish media, too, are sounding the alarm.

"Putin is sending out a signal that he is prepared to kill our citizens," Bartosz Wielinski wrote in the Tuesday edition of the Polish daily Gazeta Wyborcza. The Kremlin, he wrote, had sent a message that Poland is "the next country in line."
"These are no longer arson attacks or cyberattacks. These are acts on the threshold of war," he wrote.
Polish daily Rzeczpospolita said that "Putin is knocking on NATO's door."

"The attack on the Warsaw–Kyiv railway line was not just another Russian provocation. It was an attempt to intimidate Poland and the West. The response from Poland's politicians will show whether they are capable of assuming responsibility for the country's security," wrote editor-in-chief Michal Szuldrzynski.

Incidents involving Russian drones are now almost a daily occurrence in Poland. On Monday, a drone washed up on a beach near Jaroslawiec on the Baltic coast. A preliminary investigation indicates that the aircraft was unarmed and appeared to be intended for reconnaissance rather than combat.
"We do not know where Russia believes the limits of the escalation spiral lie," Kosiniak-Kamysz said. "But we do know that the Russians are prepared to go even further."
This article was originally published in German.

International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner on Wednesday said they are not inclined to adopt the arrangement proposed by the Registry to conduct blocks of hearings with breaks and sitting hours in the trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte.
“The Registry has taken the view that we’re going to have what has become, I’m afraid, ultra common in this court, sitting schedule then breaks,” she said during the third status conference.
“At the moment, we are not minded to do that. We are intending to sit through— we start on November 30th and then end, I think, it’s the middle of the week. Before the Christmas break,” she added.
Korner stressed the need for the trial to proceed as quickly as possible.
Duterte’s trial is scheduled to begin on November 30.
He is facing crimes against humanity charges over alleged killings during his time as President and Davao City mayor.
He attended his status conference for the first time. He was arrested in March 2025 at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3.
The former leader is currently detained at the ICC Detention Centre in Scheveningen in The Hague, The Netherlands.
He attended his status conference for the first time Wednesday.
Duterte sat behind his defense team. In the few moments that the former official was shown in the livestream, he appeared to be listening to the proceedings. —LDF, GMA News
